name: Volders
kurzbeschreibung: Historic community in the Unterinntal with the baroque Schloss Friedberg and the largest herb garden in Tirol.
beschreibung:
Overview

Volders is situated at an elevation of 558 meters in the lower Tyrolean Inn Valley on the southern bank of the Inn River, approximately 15 kilometers east of Innsbruck in the district of Innsbruck-Land. Home to around 4,540 residents, this historic village of castles and culture lies directly opposite the medieval salt-mining town of Hall in Tirol within the Hall-Wattens vacation region. At the southern fringe of the village opens the pristine 14-kilometer Voldertal valley, penetrating deep into the peaks of the Tux Alps, including Mount Glungezer, Naviser Jöchl, and Rosenjoch. Volders is renowned for its remarkable concentration of aristocratic heritage sites—such as Schloss Friedberg castle and Ansitz Aschach—as well as the iconic Karlskirche church with its unmistakable domed silhouette gracing the riverbank.

History

Traces of human settlement reach back to the Bronze and Urnfield eras; on the nearby forested hill of Himmelreich, an important fortified Rhaetian hill settlement flourished between the 4th and 1st centuries BC, now preserved as an open-air archaeological park. Volders was first recorded in writing in 995 AD under the name 'Volares'. The village commanded strategic importance due to its bridge over the Inn and its fortified manor seats: Schloss Friedberg was constructed around 1230 by the Counts of Andechs and later expanded into a magnificent Renaissance residence from 1491 by the wealthy Fieger patrician family of Hall. Architecturally unique in Austria is the Karlskirche on the riverbank: between 1620 and 1654, the court physician and polymath Dr. Hippolyt Guarinoni erected North Tyrol's first Baroque central-plan church, distinguished by a cloverleaf layout and six oriental-style domes. Its interior features luminous Rococo ceiling frescoes executed around 1765 by master Martin Knoller. Deep in the Voldertal, the historical mineral spa Volderwildbad operated from 1463, celebrated for its curative springs studied by Guarinoni.

Getting There

By car, Volders is reached via the Inntal Autobahn A12 at the Hall Mitte/Ost or Wattens exit, or along the parallel B171 state highway. Train passengers utilize Volders-Baumkirchen station on the Lower Inn Valley railway: S-Bahn lines S1 and S2 as well as regional REX trains connect the station every half hour to Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof in just twelve minutes. Frequent VVT regional bus routes 4123 and 4125 provide seamless service between Innsbruck, Hall, Volders, and Wattens.

Tips

A tour of the Karlskirche church in Volders is essential to admire its distinctive six-domed skyline and the radiant Rococo ceiling frescoes painted by Martin Knoller. An idyllic cultural walk climbs from the Karlskirche past the Renaissance manor of Ansitz Aschach to Schloss Friedberg, offering vistas of the Inn Valley before continuing to the Rhaetian open-air museum at Himmelreich. Hikers can journey into the untouched Voldertal starting from Volderwildbad, walking up to the rustic Voldertalhütte alpine refuge at 1,376 meters or exploring high pastures below Mount Glungezer.
